why: The library table's heap rows for splice and slice count a negative start from the end, as the spec does; before this pair they clamped it to 0, so xs.splice(-1, 1) proved equal to xs.splice(0, 1). dropLast changes the start from -1 to 0 (unproved, WITNESS on an array of two or more: the array left behind differs, the length agrees); tail changes slice(-2) to slice(0, 2) (unproved, WITNESS); trimEnd writes the same removal with a negative start and with xs.length - 1 (proved, PASS-bounded); head is untouched. Lane B's content check for splice compares the receiver after the call with the spec's result, so a wrong row is a defect it reports.
